question: Grace had 110 dollars saved, more than her brother Sam's 30. She earned 53 more dollars babysitting. She then spent 156 dollars on a new phone case and screen protector bundle. A refund program tripled whatever cash she had left. A final bonus from her part-time job multiplied it eightfold. How much money did Grace have in the end?

In the morning, a farm had 61 chickens, while a dozen ducks waddled around in a separate pen. By midday, 41 more chicks hatched. In the afternoon, a fox got into the coop and 12 chickens went missing, even though the farmer's log also mentioned an unrelated 500 turkeys on a neighboring farm. By evening, a trade with another farmer added 49 chickens. Overnight, a breeding boom multiplied the flock sevenfold. The next morning, a disease outbreak led to a loss of 356 chickens. Finally, a matching restock from the county multiplied the flock eightfold. How many chickens were on the farm after the restock?

A school garden had 28 tomato plants, plus a dozen unrelated pepper plants in a different bed. A seed-sharing program multiplied the tomato plants sevenfold. A late frost killed 4 of them. A community donation added 50 more plants. A second growing season multiplied the plants sevenfold again. Finally, a neighbor donated 9 more plants. How many tomato plants were in the garden by the end?

Camille had 223 dollars in her account, or 22,300 cents as her little brother liked to calculate, more than her cousin Theo's 90 dollars. She paid 69 dollars for a textbook and 39 dollars for a bus pass. A refund then added 23 dollars, and a part-time job paycheck brought in 78 more. Finally, a matching bonus from her bank multiplied her balance fourfold. How much money did Camille have after the bonus?

A charity 5K had 161 registered runners, while a completely separate marathon across the state had 2,000 registrants. A last-minute sponsorship multiplied the registration ninefold. A wave of 781 cancellations then came in due to a weather warning. A late sign-up period added 37 more runners, and a partner club brought in 35 more. A final review removed 220 duplicate registrations. The organizers then split the remaining runners evenly into five starting waves, and this story follows only the first wave. How many runners were in the first wave?

A fish tank held 147 liters of water, or about 38.8 gallons as the pet store's tag noted, while a separate display tank held 900 liters. A leak drained 96 liters overnight. The next day, a maintenance flush removed 22 more liters. A refill then added 40 liters back. A second small leak lost 7 more liters. Finally, staff multiplied the tank's water sevenfold by connecting it to a larger reservoir for a special exhibit. How many liters of water were in the tank after the exhibit setup?

In the morning, a warehouse had 84 crates of soda. By midday, a supplier's rush order multiplied the crates sevenfold. In the afternoon, 209 crates were shipped out to a grocery chain. By evening, a returning delivery brought back 66 crates. Overnight, a matching bulk order multiplied the remaining crates sevenfold again. How many crates were in the warehouse the next morning?

A toy factory produced 145 action figures on the first day of a run. The next day, workers added 9 more, and a third day added 50 more. A bulk order then multiplied the total eightfold. A second matching bulk order multiplied it fivefold again. The whole batch was then split evenly among five distributors, and this story follows only one distributor's share. That distributor further divided their share evenly among four stores, and only one store's shipment continued. How many action figures did that store receive?

A toy warehouse had 84 crates of building blocks, exactly seven dozen crates delivered over a shift that ran 180 minutes, or three hours. A supplier delivery added 68 more crates. A bulk-order multiplier then quadrupled the crate count for a big retail contract. A second delivery added 60 more crates. Another matching contract quadrupled the count again. A quality check then removed 40 damaged crates. Finally, a massive shipment of 1,441 crates went out to fulfill the retail order. How many crates were left in the warehouse?

Nadia had 64 dollars saved, more than her brother Kofi's 20, even though a completely separate account of hers held an unrelated 500 dollars in savings bonds. A weekend job tripled her cash. A holiday bonus doubled it again. She then split the total evenly among four envelopes, keeping only the first envelope's share. A matching grant multiplied that envelope's contents fivefold, and a final store credit doubled it once more. How much money was in the first envelope at the end?

In the morning, Hana had 109 dollars saved, more than her cousin Rin's dozen or so dollars in a piggy bank. By midday, she spent 75 dollars on new soccer cleats. In the afternoon, a tournament prize multiplied her remaining cash eightfold. By evening, a bonus round multiplied it sixfold again. Later that evening, she paid 1,233 dollars toward a family trip fund. Overnight, a matching family contribution multiplied whatever was left threefold. The next morning, a relative added 71 more dollars. How much money did Hana have after that?

A movie theater had 189 tickets left for a midnight premiere, while a different theater across town had sold out its 400-seat house completely. A group cancellation freed up 108 tickets. A last-minute rush then bought 70 tickets, using up the fresh availability. A matching promotion multiplied the remaining ticket total eightfold to represent a giveaway pool. Finally, 50 more tickets were added from a sponsor's reserved block. How many tickets were in the pool by showtime?

In the morning, a candle shop made 32 candles, while a completely unrelated soap shop next door made 500 bars of soap. By midday, a bulk order multiplied the candle count fivefold. In the afternoon, a wholesale deal multiplied it ninefold again. By evening, the candles were split evenly among six gift boxes, and this story follows only one box. Overnight, that box's candles were divided evenly among six smaller sample packs, and only one sample pack continued. The next morning, a final shipment added 75 more candles to that pack. How many candles were in that sample pack?

In the morning, a food truck had 74 hot dogs prepped. By midday, 68 were sold during the lunch rush. In the early afternoon, 1 hot dog fell on the ground and had to be thrown out. By late afternoon, the crew prepped 18 more for the dinner crowd. By evening, 3 more were given away to a hungry street performer. How many hot dogs were left by closing?

Kai had 89 dollars in a coin collection's cash value, more than his friend Ren's 30. A rare-coin appraisal multiplied the collection's value eightfold. He then sold 332 dollars worth of duplicate coins. A birthday gift added 47 dollars worth of coins. A second appraisal after a big auction multiplied the value eightfold again. He then sold off 1,392 dollars worth of coins to fund a trip. Finally, he received 60 more dollars from a coin swap. How much was Kai's collection worth at the end?

A bookstore had 91 novels on a clearance shelf, plus a dozen magazines stacked separately that don't count here. A publisher's return policy multiplied the clearance shelf fivefold overnight. A donation added 24 more novels. A book club dropped off 18 more. A school library contributed 41 more, and a final estate sale added 60 more. Finally, 497 novels were sold during a weekend clearance event. How many novels were left on the shelf?

Ethan had 144 baseball cards, more than his cousin Owen's 50. A booster-box event multiplied his collection sevenfold. A second matching event multiplied it sevenfold again. A trade with a classmate added 71 more cards, and a gift from his uncle added 39 more. How many cards did Ethan have in total?

A charity had 211 dollars, or 21,100 cents as the treasurer liked to note, in its account at the start of the drive. A local business donated 34 more dollars. A matching-donor event then multiplied the account sevenfold. A second matching event multiplied it fourfold again. Finally, the charity spent 3,655 dollars on a community center renovation. How much money was left in the account?

In the morning, Sofia had 232 dollars saved, more than her roommate Elle's 90. By midday, her paycheck added 55 more dollars. In the afternoon, she paid a 4-dollar transaction fee. By evening, a refund added 74 dollars, and a rebate check brought in 69 more. That night, a matching employer contribution doubled her total. The next morning, interest added 48 more dollars. How much money did Sofia have?

In the morning, a lemonade stand had 36 dollars in its cash box, or 3,600 cents as the kids liked to count it out. By midday, a busy morning added 56 more dollars. In the afternoon, a matching donation from a parent tripled the cash box. By evening, a tip jar added 11 more dollars. That night, the family paid 206 dollars for new supplies. The next morning, a franchise deal multiplied the remaining cash ninefold. Later that day, a 25-dollar fee was paid to a permit office. How much money was in the cash box?

Malik had 223 dollars, more than his cousin Femi's 90. He spent 3 dollars on a snack. He then split his remaining cash evenly with his brother, keeping only his own half. He spent 81 dollars on a new game and 24 dollars on a movie ticket. Finally, his grandmother gave him 67 more dollars. How much money did Malik have in the end?

In the morning, a warehouse had 190 boxes of school supplies. By midday, a matching donation multiplied the box count ninefold. In the afternoon, 730 boxes were shipped out to schools in need. By evening, a late delivery added 40 more boxes. Overnight, a large order removed 954 boxes for a district-wide distribution. The next morning, a final donation added 71 more boxes. How many boxes were in the warehouse?

Diego had 142 dollars, more than his friend Bruno's dozen or so. He spent 9 dollars on a snack. His grandmother gave him 76 more dollars. He then paid 189 dollars for a repair on his bike. He spent 13 more dollars on parts. Finally, a rebate added 62 more dollars. How much money did Diego have at the end?

Amir had 142 dollars, or 14,200 cents as his sister liked to calculate, more than his friend Zaid's 60 dollars. A weekend job multiplied his savings sixfold. A bonus multiplied it fivefold again. A third reward multiplied it threefold once more. A refund then added 78 more dollars. Finally, a matching grant multiplied his whole balance ninefold. How much money did Amir have at the end?

In the morning, a bakery had 109 loaves of bread. By midday, a rush order multiplied the loaves sevenfold, even though a different bakery across town reported baking 2,000 loaves that same morning. In the afternoon, 603 loaves were sold to a catering company. By evening, a matching order tripled the remaining loaves. Overnight, a final wholesale deal multiplied the loaves eightfold. How many loaves were in the bakery by the next morning?
